sentences.text: Sima Karamkar @ Sima Karmakar vs The State Of Jharkhand ....

Opposite ... on 16 May, 2024
Author: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi
Bench: Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi
 In The High Court Of Jharkhand, Ranchi
 A.B.A. No. 2664 of 2024
 ----
Sima Karamkar @ Sima Karmakar .... Petitioner
-- Versus --
 The State of Jharkhand .... Opposite Party
 ----
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi

--- 
For the Petitioner :- Mr. Devesh Ajmani, Advocate For the State :- Mr. Rajneesh Vardhan, Advocate
----
2/16.05.2024

Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as the learned counsel for the
State.

2.  The petitioner is apprehending his arrest in connection with Olidih (Mango) P.S. Case No.54 of 2024, for the offence registered under sections 376, 313, 506 and 34 of the IPC, pending in the court of learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Jamshedpur.
3.
Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner is mother of Sumit Nayak and there is allegation of allegedly establishing relationship with the informant by Sunit Nayak.
He submits that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in the present case.
4. Learned State counsel opposed the prayer on the ground that the allegations are there and the matter is arising out of section 376 IPC.

5. Considering that the petitioner is mother of Sumit Nayak and the alleged relationship was established by Sumit Nayak who is son of this petitioner, and in the attending facts and circumstances, I am inclined to provide privilege of anticipatory bail to the petitioner.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the petitioner, above named, is hereby directed to surrender before the learned court within three weeks from today, and in the event of her surrender/arrest, the petitioner, above named, shall be released on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.25,000/- (Rupees Twenty Five Thousand), with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Judicial Magistrate, First Class, Jamshedpur, in connection with Olidih (Mango) P.S. Case No.54 of 2024,
subject to the conditions as laid down under section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

( Sanjay Kumar Dwivedi, J.) SI/
